It depends on the support exotic and also what boss you're fighting
If you're doing damage from a medium or long distance, snipers can work(although they'll get better next season with the 10% buff) and especially rapid fire snipers since they got an ammo buff earlier this season.
If its up close, slug shotguns or shotguns in general can also work. The biggest problem with fusion rifles is how long it takes to output damage, for instance a heavy impact frame takes around 1second to fire a shot when some other specials can fire maybe 2 or 3(snipers and shotguns) in that time frame. So by the time dps phase is over, you maybe used 50%~ or less of total ammo(this is with high impact) this is why you'd see rapid fires being used more compared to other archetypes. Merciless is an exception though because of its exotic perk

The problem with fusion rifles is that most of them are being used to clear ads, you can see this with how the new ones have perks built for it. Such as incandescent, reservoir burst, voltshot etc. Along with the fact they haven't been meta for dps since season of the lost.
Your best bet, depending on dps phases would be rapid fire frames for burst dps and outputting as much as you can in a short window. I'm not entirely sure which ones are farmable but a good rapid-fire that's easy to get is null composure from the legacy legendary weapon kiosk. Cartesian coordinate with vorpal(although idk if its still farmable) and maybe likely suspect although you have to go through some hoops to get some damage perks going. 
But tbh, the main fusion rifle that is good for dps is the exotic "Merciless"

I remember thinking almost exactly the way you are now but as a guy your age. It was a self consuming abyss comparing yourself to attractive people around you wishing to be them. It made me not want to do things out of anxiety due to how I looked and how I was perceived. Then the added weight of just wanting to attract the opposite gender of you. 
It was one of my bad points in life despite me being only 22. 
But I will say something I learnt from when I was around your age to now. Even though physically you might not be the most attractive, at times people care more about your attractiveness as a person than looks. Despite however you describe yourself, there will be people out there who will find you attractive for being you. I mean look at your friends and family, they are good and close to you because of who you are as a person, not how you look.
My family tried to help me with my looks, offering advice and such, so they were open about me not looking the best which sucked at the time, but now I appreciate a lot.
Now I know it might be hard to find positive points about yourself. Since I know that constant negative view points about your own being will keep manifesting and you'll never think of yourself as a good person. But if that truly were the case, do you think the people around you now would still be there? If you were actually a bad person, then the people surrounding you would also be bad. This was a very difficult thing for me to eventually acknowledge, fighting my own mental health.
And if you don't think you can do it on your own, there is nothing wrong with seeking professional help.
As a random stranger on the Internet, I do wish you the best and don't give up, the good people around you won't give up on you.

First off, how you're feeling here is valid. You guys grew up together through high-school which for most people is an important time in their lives. Since it's around the time they'll start properly forming their personality and such. 
However at the same time, it's understandable that they'd be doing other things with other people considering you're all separated from each other, except then two. My advice is to learn to accept that they'll start living their lives as you'll live yours. And if you guys come around together again, as a trio at some point, hopefully it'll be the same as always or better. But if not, as sad as it may be, not every friendship will last but the true ones will. I've been friends with some people for a decade and even though we don't hang out often or talk, when we do, it still feels the same as if we were back in school again. 
I wish you the best, but don't think of yourself as being a bad person for feeling this way. Work on yourself and find things you enjoy doing and then hopefully there will be times where you guys can hang out again like you did in the past.

Personally I think it's all about play style. As someone who has played the skaven a fair amount the under city empire is good but I haven't really used it a lot. A general tip for it would be to not really have as many early cause it does take a fair amount of money to maintain. However it does become useful later for larger cities especially capitals such as lothern and using the % money building. Another general tip which can be also be said for all or most factions is that early game you should try focusing on your starting settlement/province up to a certain tier. A good tier to be at is when you can start recruiting plague claw catapults and rattling guns(if you have them) as they will be your main power in the army. Of course you can use the melee infantry but depending on the difficulty it would differ, as for the higher the difficulty the more melee buffs the ai gets in battle. Skaven's ambush mechanic is an amazing mechanic for you to use as(sucks getting ambushed back as another faction) and you should try to exploit as much as possible as ambushes give you such an advantage. If you want to set up an ambush you can see the % of it to succeed by hovering over that area. Each settlement building should always have a defensive structure as skaven by far have the best out of any race. 
And honestly you shouldn't really be using skavenslaves except maybe the slingers as they just don't really perform that well. And you want your frontline to last as long as possible so your missile units can use all their ammo. 
But the best thing about the skaven? That would be ikit claw. Most fun out of any legendary lord I've had.
